# ECN-2026-005 Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

## Reason for change

Background: An operational review and reliability analysis of the machining induction billet heater EQ-P1-L3-IH01 identified recurring thermal imbalance events correlated with cooling water flow fluctuations. Inspection findings and vendor consultation concluded that the existing documented minimum coil cooling water flow did not reflect observed required flow rates to maintain safe coil temperatures under typical machining duty cycles. The change updates the documented minimum coil cooling water flow for the coil circuit to the value required to restore acceptable thermal margins and reduce unscheduled thermal trips and associated production disruptions.

Rationale: The change establishes a clarified minimum coil cooling water flow value to align maintenance, commissioning, and process control activities. Specifying the minimum flow in the equipment documentation removes interpretive variability between operations and maintenance teams, supports consistent alarm setpoints in the local control system, and provides a single source of truth for post-modification validation and future audits. This will reduce risk of coil overheating, early insulation degradation, and unplanned downtime.

Related documents: ECN-2026-046, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-05

## Affected items

Scope: This change applies to EQ-P1-L3-IH01 and to records and procedures that reference coil cooling water flow for that equipment. Affected items include the equipment specification sheets, the local control logic documentation, the preventive maintenance checklist referenced in SOP-P1-L3-05, and the spare parts verification procedure referenced in SB-1026. Technical drawings and tag lists that include coil cooling water requirements must be revised to reflect the updated minimum flow.

Items to be revised:
- Equipment documentation and nameplate data for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
- Maintenance work orders and checklists that cite coil cooling water minimums.
- Control system alarm and interlock setpoints that enforce coil cooling flow.
- Operator procedure steps in SOP-P1-L3-05 that refer to acceptable cooling conditions.

Examples of impacted activities:
- Commissioning and start-up verification where acceptance criteria rely on coil cooling flow.
- Shift handover checks that require operators to confirm cooling water adequacy.
- Troubleshooting guides used by maintenance that specify corrective actions for low flow conditions.

Records to keep:
- Updated equipment specification sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 with the revised minimum flow incorporated.
- Revised activity sheets and checklists from SOP-P1-L3-05 showing the updated acceptance criteria.
- As-built control logic printouts showing alarm and interlock settings changed to reflect the new minimum.
- Field verification records and test logs demonstrating compliance during implementation.
- Affected work order change logs and maintenance history entries linked to ECN-2026-005.

Mandatory note: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min.

## Implementation

Change actions:
- Revise the equipment specification sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to include the updated minimum coil cooling water flow. Ensure the mandatory note above appears verbatim in the specification and nameplate references.
- Update SOP-P1-L3-05 to reflect the new acceptance criteria and any operator checks that reference coil cooling water. Replace or annotate affected pages and ensure effective distribution to operations staff.
- Update control system documentation and implement the revised alarm and interlock setpoints in the control logic. Ensure the logic changes are reviewed and signed off per control change procedures.
- Modify maintenance checklists and preventive maintenance instructions to include flow verification against the specified minimum. Cross-reference SB-1026 where procedures require confirmation of flow-related spare parts or diagnostic steps.
- Conduct field verification testing after changes are applied. Document flow measurements and demonstrate that system performance is within acceptable ranges when coil cooling flow meets or exceeds the specified minimum. Record results in the equipment test log.
- Provide targeted training for operations and maintenance personnel that covers the reason for the change, the new documented minimum, how to verify flow, and steps to take if flow is below the specified value. Update training records to reference ECN-2026-005.

Implementation sequence:
- Issue revised documentation and circulate to affected groups referenced in SOP-P1-L3-05 and SB-1026.
- Schedule control logic change and maintenance checklist update during a planned access window to avoid unplanned production impact.
- Perform post-change verification and close ECN when records show compliance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documentation updated to include the mandatory note verbatim.
- Control logic changes implemented and verified.
- Training completed and training records filed.
- Field verification records demonstrating system operability when coil cooling flow meets the specified minimum.

Records retention:
- Place all revised documents, verification test logs, and training records in the document control system under ECN-2026-005. Cross-reference ECN-2026-046, SB-1026, and SOP-P1-L3-05 as applicable.

## Approvals

Engineering review and approval:
- Mechanical engineering to verify updated specification and maintenance implications.
- Controls engineering to approve control logic changes and alarm setpoints.
- Operations leadership to approve procedural updates in SOP-P1-L3-05 and confirm readiness for field implementation.

Approval records:
- Signed ECN approval form, with approvals recorded in the document control system.
- Control logic change approval log.
- Training completion records linked to the ECN document id.

Post-implementation review:
- A post-implementation review meeting will be conducted to assess operational performance and any residual issues. Field verification records and any deviation reports will be appended to the ECN record package.

Related documents: ECN-2026-046, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-05

End of change notice.
